entries.title: Covenant Finances
entries.summary: Introduces the optional detailed covenant finance rules for troupes who want stories about increasing wealth or threats to income.
quotes: Covenants almost always need some source of mundane wealth to obtain things like food and clothing.

entries.title: The Mythic Pound
entries.summary: Defines the Mythic Pound, the standard currency used in the covenant finance rules.
quotes: One Mythic Pound is equivalent to a pound of silver, the annual income of a typical peasant, or enough money to maintain an average Hermetic laboratory for a year.

versions.title: The Mythic Pound
versions.summary: Defines the abstract currency unit used for all covenant prices and accounting, so troupes need not track differing local coinages.
quotes: One Mythic Pound is equivalent to a pound of silver, the annual income of a typical peasant, or enough money to maintain an average Hermetic laboratory for a year.

entries.title: Covenant Income
entries.summary: A covenant's income comes from one or more sources of income, each ranked in one of four categories by how much it yields.
quotes: Each source of income comes in one of four categories, specifying broadly how much income it provides (see insert).

entries.title: Source of Income Categories
entries.summary: Table of the none, Lesser, Typical, Greater and Legendary income categories with the Hook or Boon tied to each and its typical annual income in pounds.

entries.title: Baseline Income
entries.summary: A standard covenant has one Typical source of income (or two Lesser), and the income is adjusted per magus above or below a six-magus covenant.
quotes: you may wish to adjust the income upwards by 15 pounds per additional magus

entries.title: Covenant Expenditure
entries.summary: Explains how to work out normal yearly expenditure from covenfolk, weapons and armor and laboratory points, add sundry expenses, and apply the surplus or shortfall to the covenant's stores.
quotes: To start with, you should determine the normal yearly expenditure of the covenant

entries.title: Covenfolk Categories
entries.summary: Sorts covenfolk into craftsmen, dependents, grogs, laborers, servants, specialists and teamsters for accounting, and gives the procedure for the minimum number of servants and teamsters.
quotes: Number of Servants required: 2 for every 10 points of (all inhabitants, excluding laborers, servants, and teamsters)
Number of Teamsters required: 1 for every 10 points of

entries.title: Points for Inhabitants of a Typical Covenant
entries.summary: Table of expenditure points per inhabitant type (magus, companion, specialist, other covenfolk, horse) with the Living Conditions modifier by covenant season, and how impoverished magi can reduce their point cost.
quotes: impoverished magi may reduce their point cost to 3

entries.title: Points of Laboratories
entries.summary: Converts each laboratory's Upkeep score into expenditure points, with a usage multiplier for maintenance, and a rule for Upkeep scores above +5.
quotes: For example, a standard laboratory (Upkeep 0) equates to 10 points.
the number of extra points gained per level of Upkeep increase is equal to the new Upkeep score times ten

entries.title: Points of Weapons and Armor
entries.summary: Table giving expenditure points for weapons, armor and siege engines at Inexpensive, Standard and Expensive quality, totalled across the covenant.
quotes: Add up the points of the weapons and armor possessed by all the characters at the covenant

entries.title: Yearly Expenditure Categories
entries.summary: Introduces the categories of regular yearly expenditure and a rule of thumb relating a covenant's affordable inhabitant points to its income.
quotes: a covenant can afford a number of points of inhabitants equal to its income in pounds

entries.title: Buildings Expenditure
entries.summary: Yearly cost of maintaining the covenant's buildings, plus extra for Boons that add to its buildings or fortifications.
quotes: Buildings cost: 1 pound for every 10 points of inhabitants.

entries.title: Consumables Expenditure
entries.summary: Yearly cost of tools, candles, fuel and other consumables for the covenant.
quotes: CONSUMABLES COST: 2 pounds for every 10 points of inhabitants.

entries.title: Laboratories Expenditure
entries.summary: Yearly cost of maintaining the covenant's laboratories, based on their points from Upkeep scores.
quotes: LABORATORIES COST: 1 pound per 10 points of laboratories.

entries.title: Provisions Expenditure
entries.summary: Yearly cost of food and fodder, usually the largest item of covenant expenditure.
quotes: PROVISIONS COST: 5 pounds for every 10 points of inhabitants.

entries.title: Wages
entries.summary: Yearly cost of covenfolk stipends and magi allowances; changing the standard wages changes covenfolk Loyalty.
quotes: WAGES COST: 2 pounds for every 10 points of inhabitants.

entries.title: Weapons and Armor Expenditure
entries.summary: Yearly cost of cleaning, repairing and replacing the covenant's weapons and armor.
quotes: WEAPONS AND ARMOR COST: 1 pound for every 320 points of weapons and armor.

entries.title: Writing Materials Expenditure
entries.summary: Yearly cost of parchment and ink, assuming one pound writes four books without embellishment.
quotes: WRITING MATERIALS COST: 1 pound for every magus, scribe, bookbinder, or illuminator.

entries.title: Cost Saving
entries.summary: A covenant can cut expenditure by employing laborers, employing craftsmen, or using magical items and Ritual spells that substitute for human work.
quotes: by employing laborers, by employing craftsmen, and by utilizing magical items (or Ritual spells) which substitute for the work of one or more humans

entries.title: Cost Saving by Craftsmen
entries.summary: Common and rare craftsmen reduce expenditure according to their Craft Ability, subject to a per-craft limit in each expenditure category.
quotes: A common craftsman reduces expenditure by a number of pounds equal to one plus half of his Craft Ability, rounded down.
A rare craftsman reduces expenditure by a number of pounds equal to his Craft Ability.

entries.title: Yearly Expenditure Summary
entries.summary: One-page summary of every yearly expenditure formula.
quotes: Inhabitants: 1 pound per point of inhabitants
INFLATION: Starts at 0; increases by an average of 1 pound per 100 pounds of expenditure per year

versions.title: Yearly Expenditure Summary
versions.summary: One-page summary of every yearly expenditure formula and cost-saving rule, for quick reference when totalling a covenant's costs.
quotes: Ritual spells: For each magnitude of effect, subtract 5 pounds
Magic items: For each magnitude of effect, subtract 1 pound

entries.title: Cost Saving Summary
entries.summary: Summary of the per-unit cost saving formulas for laborers, craftsmen, magic items and Ritual spells, and of the cost saving limits.
quotes: Craftsmen (common): For each, subtract 1 + (Ability / 2) pounds (rounding down)

entries.title: Expenditure - A Simple Example
entries.summary: Worked example of computing inhabitant points, servants, teamsters and yearly expenditure for a starting covenant and again after ten years of expansion with cost savings.
quotes: It thus needs 12 servants (12 points), taking the total to 70 points.

entries.title: Wealth and Poverty: Rounding and Starting Money
entries.summary: Opening rules for covenant finances: round major income and expenditure to whole pounds and ignore small amounts, an autocrat or magus oversees the treasury, and a starting cash reserve can be bought with Build Points.
quotes: Round any major income or expenditure to the nearest pound, and disregard smaller amounts (shillings and pence).
(at the rate of one Build Point per 10 pounds)

entries.title: Customizing Income Sources
entries.summary: Shows how the Hooks and Boons chosen at covenant creation determine how many sources of income the covenant has and of what category.
quotes: has one Greater and one Typical source of income, with the Greater source being contested.

entries.title: Improving or Reducing Income Each Year
entries.summary: Each year the storyguide picks an effect from the Income Modification table for each source and applies its multiplier, usually permanently; success or neglect by the characters can grow or cut income.
quotes: Each year, the storyguide should choose an appropriate effect according to the Income Modification table (see insert), and apply the relevant multiplier to that year's income from the source.
five years of Expansion results in a Typical source of income growing to become equivalent to a Greater source.

entries.title: Income Modification Table
entries.summary: Table of yearly effects on a source of income (Slump to Boom), each with an income multiplier and the stress die result used if the effect is rolled randomly.
quotes: | Status Quo | x 1 | 3–8 |

entries.title: Sundry Expenses
entries.summary: Irregular one-off yearly expenses such as travel, Redcap fees, equipment, buildings, land and lab upgrades, tracked separately from regular expenditure.

entries.title: The Pound of Enumerus
entries.summary: A fixed extra amount of undocumented spending that is added to sundry expenses every year, and may be higher for a cursed or badly managed covenant.
quotes: Every year, therefore, you should add one pound onto the sundry expenses.

entries.title: Sources of Income
entries.summary: A list of kinds of income source (agriculture, charity, crime, fishing, trade, wizardry and so on) that can inspire a covenant, any of which can supply any level of income.
quotes: any source can supply any level of income

versions.title: Sources of Income (general rules)
versions.summary: General rules for choosing and running sources of income: which need the Right Boon or Contested/Indiscreet Resource Hooks, why goods must be sold carefully, and that operating costs are already deducted from the income figure.
quotes: it is not sufficient merely to produce the good in question, it must also be sold, either for other goods or cash.
the income provided by the source is simply the surplus after such "operating costs" have been deducted.

entries.title: Inflation
entries.summary: A flat yearly cost added to expenditure to model the covenant's corrosive effect on local prices; it starts at zero and rises each year.
quotes: it is suggested that it increase by one pound per hundred pounds of expenditure every year

entries.title: Tithes
entries.summary: Yearly payments to another covenant, a feudal overlord, the Church or creditors, set by the covenant's situation and the saga.
quotes: The amount of these obligations is determined by the situation of the covenant, and development of the saga.

entries.title: Cost Saving by Laborers
entries.summary: Each laborer reduces Provisions expenditure, up to a cap of half of the Provisions total.
quotes: Each laborer working for the covenant reduces expenditure on Provisions by one pound.

versions.title: Cost Saving by Laborers
versions.summary: How much each laborer saves on Provisions and the cap on total savings from laborers alone.
quotes: Each laborer working for the covenant reduces expenditure on Provisions by one pound.
The maximum amount of money that can be saved by laborers is half of the Provisions total.

entries.title: Cost Saving Limits by Craft
entries.summary: Table of example craftsmen and the maximum percentage of each expenditure category that any one craft can save.
quotes: stonemason, carpenter, furniture maker, thatcher

entries.title: Cost Saving by Magic
entries.summary: Magic items and Ritual spells can substitute for covenfolk or supplies, saving money per magnitude of effect at the storyguide's discretion.
quotes: each magnitude of effect in such items can save one pound per year
Each casting of a Ritual spell may save approximately five pounds per magnitude

entries.title: Emergency Savings
entries.summary: Options when expenditure exceeds income: privileged members give up perks, wages are cut, covenfolk are laid off, or categories are neglected, each with Loyalty and story consequences.
quotes: If you have fewer than these minimums, it will adversely affect the functioning of the covenant

entries.title: Tips for a Smoothly Run Covenant
entries.summary: Practical advice on keeping covenant records: shared notes, delegated library, vis and finance tracking, vis tokens, an annual calendar and a covenant logbook.

entries.title: Magical Improvement of Income
entries.summary: Covers using magic to raise covenant income, its three drawbacks (lab time and vis, unwanted attention, local inflation), Tribunal limits on creating silver, and the storyguide choosing a one-off permanent income multiplier.
quotes: several of the Tribunals have recently passed measures limiting each covenant to the creation of at most 2 pounds of silver (or its equivalent) per magus per year
The storyguide should decide upon the effectiveness of any magical improvement a covenant undertakes and choose an appropriate income multiplier

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, page 87

entries.title: Income Source: Agriculture
entries.summary: Farming as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Charity
entries.summary: Regular gifts from a donor as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Crime
entries.summary: Banditry, smuggling and similar crime as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Fishing
entries.summary: Fishing and whaling as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Forestry
entries.summary: Timber, fur and hunting as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Hospitality
entries.summary: Inns, taverns and similar businesses as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Livestock
entries.summary: Herding for wool, hides and meat as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Manufacturing
entries.summary: Craft production of goods as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Mining
entries.summary: Mines and quarries as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Money
entries.summary: Moneylending, banking and pawnbroking as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Service
entries.summary: Hiring out skilled covenfolk or companions as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Toll-Gathering
entries.summary: Charging tolls at a bridge, ford or pass as a covenant income source; needs ownership or permission, enforcement, and usually the Right Boon.

entries.title: Income Source: Trade
entries.summary: Moving goods from where they are cheap to where they are dear as a covenant income source, with pros, cons, magical options and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Income Source: Wizardry
entries.summary: Selling magical services, items, or Hermetic goods such as books, lab texts, vis and longevity rituals as a covenant income source, with pros, cons and example sources at each size category.

entries.title: Expenditure Worked Example (Semita Errabunda)
entries.summary: Worked example of a larger covenant's income and expenditure, including cost savings from laborers, craftsmen and magic items that stand in for servants.
quotes: two magic items with a total of 4 magnitudes of effects take the place of 4 servants

entries.title: The Price of Vis
entries.summary: Explains why vis has no fixed silver price and gives a base guideline for the rare cases where it is bought or sold for silver.
quotes: a base guideline of roughly ten pounds per pawn is a reasonable rule of thumb for a typical saga.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, page 87

entries.title: Sundry Expense: Books
entries.summary: Costs for buying mundane books and for decorating Hermetic books with resonant materials.
quotes: a good rule of thumb is that these precious materials cost one pound per book

entries.title: Sundry Expense: Hermetic Commodities
entries.summary: Hermetic goods traded between magi are normally priced in vis, with cash accepted only exceptionally.
quotes: are almost always priced in vis, not silver

entries.title: Sundry Expense: Hospitality
entries.summary: Costs of hosting Redcaps, noble or magus guests, and festivals, which can also add Loyalty points.
quotes: It is customary that each visiting Redcap is paid 30 silver pennies (an eighth of a pound) for her services.

entries.title: Sundry Expense: Laboratory Construction
entries.summary: Cost to outfit a new laboratory or to raise its Upkeep, based on the laboratory's points.
quotes: cost one pound per two points of the laboratory

entries.title: Sundry Expense: Magi
entries.summary: Major personal purchases by magi are added to sundry expenses; minor spending is already covered by the wages allowance.

entries.title: Sundry Expense: Property
entries.summary: Buying land or building new property: land needed per farmhand, building time per floor, a surcharge to build faster, and building cost tied to the points of inhabitants housed.
quotes: roughly one virgate of arable land (a twentieth of a square mile) is needed for each farmhand laborer at the covenant
it takes one year per floor (or ten feet of height) to build.
This rate can be doubled by paying 50% more.

entries.title: Sundry Expense: Training
entries.summary: Paying outsiders to train covenfolk costs a fraction of what the same skilled person costs to employ.
quotes: assume that a skilled individual costs half as much to recruit for teaching as to employ for work

entries.title: Sundry Expense: Travel
entries.summary: Travel and accommodation costs for expeditions; rough travel needs no accounting but may cost a season's Living Conditions modifier.
quotes: If such a party is traveling rough, however, then you need not account for their expenses

entries.title: Technological Cost Saving
entries.summary: How magic can cut a covenant's yearly costs: each laborer replaced saves a pound of Provisions, and the food bill, being the largest share of the cost per inhabitant point, offers the most saving, especially bread; wages and consumables are harder to cut.
quotes: it costs one Mythic Pound to support one point of inhabitants
Half this cost — i.e. 10 shillings — is taken up by provisions.

entries.title: Storage and Loss of Magically-Created Grain
entries.summary: Magically created grain spoils like ordinary grain: a yearly percentage is lost to rot and vermin, more without precautions, while each inhabitant point consumes a fixed number of bushels a year; a worked example shows how long a store lasts.
quotes: A peasant in Mythic Europe requires about 24 bushels of grain each year to support his nutritional needs.
the loss rate can be 5 to 10 per cent

entries.title: Supply Shortage in Laboratories
entries.summary: Rules for a lab supply shortage that halves lab capacity: with core rules the number of active labs is cut, and with the Covenants lab rules the total Upkeep is halved by taking Flaws or removing Virtues. Labs shut down completely if the shortage lasts four seasons.
quotes: the shortage means that the number of active labs must be reduced to half (round down)

entries.title: Imperial Toll Levels
entries.summary: A table of the emperor's set toll per vessel type, the daily income a toll station can expect from passing traffic, and the need for armed enforcement against rivals and toll-runners.
quotes: Small rowboat (5 persons or less) — 1d
Large ship (two or more masts) — 12d
providing a daily income of 10 schillings or more

entries.title: Covenfolk: Characters Versus Purchased Specialists
entries.summary: Covenfolk can be bought as specialists with Build Points, which gives them Abilities but no character sheet, or created as grogs or companions, which costs no Build Points; the chapter recommends real characters and suits slow and medium saga speeds best.
quotes: Characters created as grogs or companions, however, need not be paid for with Build Points.

entries.title: The Organization of Covenfolk
entries.summary: Introduces the models (hierarchy, nations, guilds, no structure) around which a covenant's grogs and covenfolk can be organized, which may be mixed.
quotes: Naturally it is possible to mix-and-match

entries.title: Hierarchy
entries.summary: A hierarchy is the most common organization and least work for the magi; the two main models are the noble household and the military.
quotes: The two most significant hierarchical models adopted are those of the noble household and the military.

entries.title: A Noble Household
entries.summary: Covenfolk organized like a noble household under a steward, chamberlain and marshal, and what each official controls.
quotes: the three chief officials in a noble household are the steward, the chamberlain, and the marshal

entries.title: Military Hierarchy
entries.summary: Covenfolk divided into squads of soldiers and auxiliary staff, suited to military covenants or covenants split over several sites.
quotes: the covenfolk are divided into squads, each of which consists of soldiers and their auxiliary staff

entries.title: Nations
entries.summary: Covenfolk organized into cross-role nations by lot, sponsor, contest or birth; members may have a Loyalty Trait to their nation as well as the covenant.
quotes: Members of nations often have a Loyalty Personality Trait specific to the nation as well as to the covenant.

entries.title: Guilds
entries.summary: Covenfolk organized by function into guilds, from the basic servant/specialist/soldier split to many finer groups, often self-organizing.
quotes: An alternative to nations is guilds; that is, organizing the grogs by their function.

entries.title: Professional Guilds
entries.summary: A covenant organization modeled on craft and merchant guilds with a dean, aldermen, masters, journeymen and apprentices.
quotes: At the head of a guild is the dean, elected by the guild members from among their number.

entries.title: Monastery
entries.summary: A guild-like model in which an abbot designates officials who manage each department and can call on others for help; good for small covenants.
quotes: the abbot of a monastery designates officials to manage each aspect of the daily life of the monastery

entries.title: No Formal Structure
entries.summary: A small covenant with no formal organization, which risks neglected tasks unless the covenfolk form a cohesive group.
quotes: This is usually only possible for very small numbers of covenfolk

entries.title: Rivalries and Tension
entries.summary: Any social structure can breed rivalry between nations, guilds, families, or officials such as the steward, chamberlain and turb captain.
quotes: A common rivalry occurs between the steward and the chamberlain over precedence

entries.title: Troupe Styles and Covenfolk
entries.summary: Shows how covenfolk fit the Alternative Characters and Pooled Characters troupe styles, how a grog can shift between them, and how easily covenfolk can be advanced in bulk.

entries.title: Magical Alternatives to Covenfolk
entries.summary: Compares replacing covenfolk with spells, enchanted devices, automata or enchanted parts of the covenant, noting the limits of each: a magus must cast spells and have the Finesse, devices cost time and vis and need a wielder, and people remain more flexible.
quotes: Rego craft magic furthermore depends on the Finesse of the casting magus

entries.title: Grex (grog squad)
entries.summary: Defines the grex as the small unit of grogs that accompanies magi on expeditions, and how greges relate to the turb as permanent or newly assembled squads.
quotes: A grex typically numbers up to six individuals

entries.title: Custos (favored grog)
entries.summary: Explains the custos, a favored grog set apart by skill, great deeds or loyalty and given better provisions and pay, and that custodes count as specialists when building a covenant and working out its finances.
quotes: Custodes are usually equated to specialists when building a covenant

entries.title: Servants
entries.summary: Describes the indoor and outdoor servants who keep a covenant running and how the Covenants book ties the number of servants and teamsters to the covenant's population, with laborers and craftsmen reducing outgoings.
quotes: two servants and one teamster are needed to support two magi, three companions, or ten soldiers

entries.title: Personal Servants
entries.summary: How a magus's personal servant differs from a specialist, how the role gives status among the covenfolk, and a table of suitable servant types for different kinds of magus.
quotes: Performing all these services for a magus is the mark of the personal servant

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.113

entries.title: The Chamberlain
entries.summary: The chamberlain coordinates the servants, is treated as a specialist, uses the Profession: Chamberlain Ability, and can raise or lower the covenfolk's Prevailing Loyalty by mediating the effects of The Gift.
quotes: Governing the servants of a covenant is covered by the Profession: Chamberlain Ability
boosts the Prevailing Loyalty of the covenfolk

entries.title: Specialists
entries.summary: Specialists are the covenfolk with focused skills beyond daily upkeep or defense, bought with covenant build points; the entry also explains when a craftsman counts as a servant rather than a specialist.
quotes: specialists are bought with covenant build points (ArM5, page 72)

entries.title: The Steward
entries.summary: The steward sees to the needs of the specialists, uses Profession: Steward (often with Leadership), and like the chamberlain can soften or aggravate the covenfolk's reaction to The Gift.
quotes: The role of steward is governed by the Profession: Steward Ability

entries.title: The Autocrat
entries.summary: Describes the autocrat, a single officer who combines the roles of chamberlain and steward and commands all non-military covenfolk.
quotes: he is in command of all the non-military covenfolk

entries.title: Soldiers
entries.summary: Soldiers defend the covenant; they need roughly equal Combat Totals to fight as a trained group, and companions are rarely counted among them. Also notes the Code of Hermes limits on lending soldiers to feudal lords.
quotes: soldiers need to train together and have roughly equal Combat Totals to fight effectively as a trained group

entries.title: The Turb Captain
entries.summary: The turb captain leads all of the covenant's soldiers, is provisioned as a specialist at least, and may be treated as a companion character even when designed as a grog.
quotes: A turb captain is provisioned as a specialist at least

entries.title: Unit Sergeants
entries.summary: Sergeants command smaller units of the turb, are chosen for loyalty and the Leadership Ability, and are treated as specialists for wages, food and lodging.
quotes: Sergeants are rewarded by being treated as specialists with respect to wages, food, and accommodation.

entries.title: Other Military Ranks
entries.summary: Describes the intermediate corporal-like rank between soldier and sergeant, represented by the Custos Social Status Virtue, and how temporary expedition roles can become semi-permanent.
quotes: This rank is represented by the Custos Social Status Virtue.

entries.title: Watch Patterns
entries.summary: Charts for single and double duty showing which watch and patrol is on duty, off duty or free at each time of day, so the storyguide can randomly determine which grogs are on watch when an event occurs.
quotes: randomly determine what patrol (night or day) and watch (first to fourth) a character is in

entries.title: Duties (watch, off duty and free time)
entries.summary: A soldier's time is split into duty, off-duty and free time, with the turb divided into day and night patrols who periodically swap, and with sub-patrols assigned to areas such as wall, gate and keep.
quotes: A soldier's time is divided into three periods: duty (or watch duty), off-duty, and free time.

entries.title: The Watches
entries.summary: Gives the named eight watches of the day and night with their start times, and explains how patrols rotate through normal sentry duty and double duty.
quotes: The 24 hours of the day are divided into eight watches of three hours each: four day watches and four night watches.

entries.title: Off Duty
entries.summary: What grogs do when off duty: drill with the drill sergeant, maintain kit, take work crews or errands, and can fit in Practice with an Ability; also covers the meals and daily ration provided.
quotes: If he gets time to himself with all this going on, a grog can put in some Practice with a particular Ability.

entries.title: Free Time
entries.summary: Free time is when grogs sleep; a grog who does not sleep during it loses a Long-Term Fatigue level until he sleeps long enough, and drinking the ration is only allowed just after coming off duty.
quotes: a grog who does not sleep in his free time suffers a Long-Term Fatigue level until he manages to sleep for at least two continuous watches

entries.title: Rewards
entries.summary: Explains how covenants reward skill, good behavior and bravery, usually through the turb captain, steward or chamberlain, who choose and announce the reward.
quotes: it is good for morale if the covenant is seen to reward skill, good behavior, initiative, and uncommon bravery

entries.title: Improved Rations
entries.summary: Better food as a reward, which if kept for a full year improves the grog's Living Conditions Modifier on aging rolls.
quotes: A grog spending a year on improved rations receives a –1 improvement to his Living Conditions Modifier when making aging rolls.

entries.title: Improved Equipment (reward)
entries.summary: Superior arms, armor or tools given as a reward, which may be of Expensive cost or give actual bonuses, and are lost if the grog is demoted.
quotes: This equipment might be Expensive rather than Standard cost

entries.title: Promotion In Rank
entries.summary: The highest reward: a grog can rise to custos, then sergeant or equivalent, and perhaps captain, chamberlain or steward, gaining better food, lodging, pay and pension.
quotes: A standard grog can be promoted to custos

entries.title: Punishments
entries.summary: How covenants discipline covenfolk in public, how corporal and privilege-withholding punishments differ, and how fair, proportionate punishment avoids losing Prevailing Loyalty while frequent or unjust punishment makes covenfolk hostile to the magi.
quotes: does not usually result in a loss of Prevailing Loyalty

entries.title: Reduction of Rations (punishment)
entries.summary: Reduced food as a punishment; seasons spent on reduced rations in a year worsen the grog's Living Conditions Modifier for aging.
quotes: A character who spends one or more season a year on reduced rations suffers a +1 penalty to his Living Conditions Modifier

entries.title: Retirement
entries.summary: Older grogs may be retired after a serious aging crisis, and a retired grog still counts as a covenant member for finances.
quotes: the grog is still counted as a member of the covenant as far as its finances go

entries.title: Pensions
entries.summary: Describes the pensions covenants give retired grogs, how rent may substitute for a pension, and the treatment of widows.
quotes: Pensions are usually half to three-quarters of their former pay.

entries.title: Sentries (watch on expedition)
entries.summary: On expedition each watch is shared by one or two men who stand one watch then rest for the next three, with no day and night patrol distinction.
quotes: There are eight watches in a day, each lasting three hours.

entries.title: Growing Used to The Gifted
entries.summary: People can grow used to a Gifted individual over time, so grogs use the covenant's Prevailing Loyalty rather than the magus's Gift penalty for Loyal rolls, with an optional system of separate Loyalty scores per magus.
quotes: An individual grog begins with a Loyal Personality Trait that is up to 3 points different from the turb's Prevailing Loyalty.

entries.title: The Death of a Grog
entries.summary: How grogs treat their dead: washing the body, the role of Extreme Unction (which can be performed by any baptized person but protects the spirit for a limited time only when performed by an ordained priest), burial in consecrated ground, and the loss of Prevailing Loyalty if magi insist a body be abandoned.
quotes: can result in the loss of Prevailing Loyalty

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.75

entries.title: Covenant Boons and Hooks (Creation Summary)
entries.summary: Explains that Boons improve the covenant and Hooks generate stories, with Major, Minor and Free kinds, and that Hooks supply the points that pay for Boons.
quotes: Thus, a covenant cannot start with more points of Boons than points of Hooks.

entries.title: The Covenant in Play: Gaining and Losing Boons and Hooks
entries.summary: After play begins the covenant gets no more Build Points; resources change through the characters' actions, and gaining a Boon should bring a matching Hook while a lost Boon becomes something to win back.
quotes: If a Boon is gained, the covenant should gain a corresponding Hook

entries.title: Paying for Choices (Boon and Hook Balance, Unknown Hook)
entries.summary: Explains how Major and Minor Boons and Hooks are paid for and balanced at creation, how the Unknown Hook works, how many Hooks a troupe should take, and how Boons and Hooks change during play.
quotes: Covenants created by troupes as homes for player character magi should balance.
The Unknown Hook is a Major Hook for balancing Boons.
select no more Hooks than you are likely to use in six months of real-time play

entries.title: Covenant Situations
entries.summary: Explains that a covenant's situation is independent of its season and power, and that situations are built from Boons and Hooks which a troupe can combine to design its own.
quotes: The situation of a covenant is largely independent of its season and power.

versions.title: Covenant Situations (Prebuilt Boon and Hook Packages)
versions.summary: A set of ready-made covenant packages (such as Autumn Power, Devoted, Expedition, Hermetic Market, Struggling, Urban and Worshipful), each a balanced list of Boons, Hooks and Free Choices that a troupe can adopt and tailor.
quotes: Each covenant situation described below is a package of Boons and Hooks that balance.

entries.title: Autumn Power Situation
entries.summary: A ready-made covenant situation for a strong Autumn covenant, listing the Hooks and Boons that represent rivals, politics and hierarchy.
quotes: Hooks: Hermetic Politics (Minor), Protector (Minor), Castle (Major), Rival (Major), Superiors (Major)

entries.title: Mundane Lord Situation
entries.summary: A covenant situation for a covenant that has become lord of mundanes, with its Hooks and Boons.
quotes: Hooks: Castle (Major), Mundane Politics (Major)

entries.title: Powerful Location Situation
entries.summary: A covenant situation for a site of great magical power, noting that the covenfolk living in the multiple auras suffer Warping.
quotes: Hooks: Monster (Minor) x2, Regio (Major)

entries.title: Struggling Situation
entries.summary: A covenant situation for a poor covenant with enemies, whose stories centre on mundane survival.
quotes: Hooks: Contested Resource (Minor), Poverty (Major)

entries.title: Urban Situation
entries.summary: A covenant situation for a covenant hidden in a regio inside a city, with its Hooks and Boons.
quotes: Hooks: Urban (Major)

entries.title: Winter Ruins Situation
entries.summary: A covenant situation for a covenant occupying the remains of a Winter covenant, whose contents matter greatly to the characters.
quotes: Hooks: Contested Resource (Minor) (x3), Monster (Major), Poverty (Minor)

entries.title: Major Site Boons
entries.summary: The Major Boons describing the covenant's site, such as an extra aura point in a limited area, a conscious space, a fantastic environment, immunity, a natural fortress, a regio, and time dilation or contraction.
quotes: The aura of a limited area of the covenant increases by one point.
Vis sources within the regio usually refresh in mundane time.

entries.title: Conversion from the Ars Magica Rules
entries.summary: How to convert covenants built with the core book's Boons and Hooks to this book's definitions, and what replaces the old Buildings and Fortifications Boons.

entries.title: Minor Site Boons
entries.summary: The Minor Boons for the covenant's site, including extra aura points (repeatable), difficult access, a healthy feature that helps aging rolls, immunity, a mystical portal, regio, seclusion, unnatural law, vast aura and vivid environment.
quotes: The players may take this Boon up to seven times, for a covenant in any magic aura up to ten.
Inhabitants with access to this feature have a +1 bonus on their aging rolls.

entries.title: Major Site Hooks
entries.summary: The Major Hooks for the covenant's site: constant mobility, a highly mutable aura, a magical disaster, a missing aura, a resident monster, a mystical road, a regio on the site, and an urban location.
quotes: If the regio is not magical, that counts as an additional Minor Hook.

entries.title: Minor Site Hooks
entries.summary: The Minor Hooks for the covenant's site, such as corrupt or faerie auras, curses, haunting, a flickering or weak aura, an unhealthy environment that worsens aging rolls, and several regio variants. Several of them may be taken as the Unknown Hook.
quotes: Subtract one point from the covenant's Magic aura.
All people regularly exposed to the environmental factor suffer a –1 penalty to their Aging rolls.

entries.title: Major Resources Boon (Wealth)
entries.summary: The Major Resources Boon upgrades one existing Typical source of income to Legendary.
quotes: One existing Typical source of income is upgraded to Legendary

entries.title: Minor Resources Boons
entries.summary: Minor Boons for covenant wealth: hidden resources, a right to collect income, secondary income, a vis grant, and a lesser Wealth boon that upgrades a Typical income to Greater.
quotes: The covenant has 250 Build Points of resources that are not immediately available to the player characters.
One existing Typical source of income is upgraded to Greater

entries.title: Major Resources Hooks
entries.summary: Major Hooks about the covenant's wealth: a crippling debt, an indiscreet (criminal) resource, a natural disaster that destroys the main source of wealth, and total poverty.
quotes: The yearly interest due on the debt alone amounts to about three quarters of the covenant's entire income

entries.title: Minor Resources Hooks
entries.summary: Minor Hooks about wealth: contested, dwindling, flawed and illusory resources, a moderate debt, an indiscreet resource, a natural disaster, poverty, regional produce and vis salary. Several give a concrete rate of loss or interest.
quotes: As a rule, one story means that the resource is available for five years.
The resource loses 10% of its original value per year
The yearly interest due on the debt is equal to about one quarter of the covenant's income

entries.title: Residents: Paying for Background Characters
entries.summary: Residents Boons and Hooks do not affect player-character preparation, and a background character who fits several Boons only needs to be paid for once.
quotes: A background character who fulfills several roles, and could be purchased with any of several Boons, needs only to be purchased once.

entries.title: Residents Free Choices
entries.summary: Free Choices for the covenant's defenders: hunters or sailors, who are paid, and peasant soldiers who serve as part of their rent.
quotes: These people need payment, a penny per day, for their service

entries.title: Major Residents Boons
entries.summary: Major Boons for covenant residents: heavy cavalry, magical soldiers and a tame nobleman, each with consequences for how neighbouring nobles react.

entries.title: Minor Residents Boons
entries.summary: Minor Boons for residents, including cavalry, crossbowmen, veteran fighters, inhuman residents, literate or loyal covenfolk (Loyal Covenfolk sets the starting Prevailing Loyalty) and a strong community.
quotes: After calculating Base Loyalty, add sufficient loyalty points to raise the Prevailing Loyalty of the covenant to +3 (30 loyalty points total).
They receive nine pence each day, even if they are not required to fight.
They receive a penny each per day, even if they are not required to fight.

entries.title: Major Residents Hooks
entries.summary: Major Hooks about residents, including Divided Loyalty (separate Prevailing Loyalty per faction) and Rebellious Covenfolk (very low starting loyalty), plus diabolic corruption, a chapter house, a school and superiors.
quotes: Actions which benefit the loyalty of one faction over the others will cause a decrease in loyalty of the other factions equal to one half of the loyalty points gained.
Subtract sufficient loyalty points to obtain a loyalty point total of –75 (a Prevailing Loyalty of –5).

entries.title: Minor Residents Hooks
entries.summary: Minor Hooks about residents, such as alienable land, dark secrets, fosterage, gender imbalance, a guild, a house church, incompetent or inhuman covenfolk, infants, spies and superiors.

entries.title: Military Preparedness
entries.summary: Lists which Residents Boons and Free Choices describe non-player fighters, noting that player characters are built with the grog or companion rules instead.
quotes: Player characters are exceptions to these general descriptions, and are created using the grog or companion rules.

entries.title: Major External Relations Boons
entries.summary: Major Boons for the covenant's dealings with outsiders, such as autocephalous status, a dedicated covenant, an exceptional book, favors owed, a hedge tradition, high Prestige and a powerful ally.
quotes: The book's (level + quality) = 35, with a maximum quality of 25 and a maximum Art level of 20.
The covenant has a Reputation score of 9.

entries.title: Minor External Relations Boons
entries.summary: Minor Boons for the covenant's dealings with outsiders: benefice, a felicitous tribunal, informants, a local ally, minor Prestige, promised favors and being ungoverned.
quotes: The covenant has a Reputation score of 3.

entries.title: Major External Relations Hooks
entries.summary: Major Hooks about outsiders: being beholden, a center of excellence, hosting Order ceremonies, a rival hedge tradition, Hermetic services, mundane politics, a rival, a tribunal border and a war zone.

entries.title: Minor External Relations Hooks
entries.summary: Minor Hooks about outsiders, such as an ancestral error, a centralized kingdom, church territories, favors owed, Hermetic politics, infamy, a public vis source, slavery and an unsafe route that Redcaps avoid.
quotes: When the saga begins, the covenant owes favors to three other covenants, but is owed three favors as well.

entries.title: Major Surroundings Boons
entries.summary: Major Boons for the covenant's surroundings: a defensive environment, tithing miracles and mystical allies.

entries.title: Minor Surroundings Boons
entries.summary: Minor Boons for the surroundings: a chase (managed royal forest), hidden ways and a minority community.

entries.title: Major Surroundings Hooks
entries.summary: Major Hooks for the surroundings, such as a nearby city, demonic interest, an enclosed covenant, a faerie landlord, a meddlesome saint, a monster, pagans, a pilgrimage site, a ruined covenant and a seat of power.

entries.title: Minor Surroundings Hooks
entries.summary: Minor Hooks for the surroundings, such as death prophecies, a faerie court, a fated feat, a festival, a ford, guardians, heretics, a legendary or massacre site, a monastery, a protectorate, sanctuary and an ungarrisoned castle.

entries.title: Table of Boons and Hooks
entries.summary: Quick-reference table listing every Boon, Free Choice and Hook with its category (Site, Buildings, Resources, Residents, External, Surroundings), whether it is Major or Minor, and any prerequisite such as the Castle Hook. Bold and italic entries mark low- and high-fantasy suitability.
quotes: Entries in bold are particularly suited to low fantasy campaigns.

entries.title: The Covenant in Play
entries.summary: Covenants gain no Build Points in play; Boons and Hooks are gained and lost through events, a gained Boon brings a matching Hook, and resolving a Hook takes many stories.
quotes: Covenants do not gain Build Points while they are being played.
it should take at least half a dozen stories for a minor Hook, and around twenty for a major Hook

entries.title: Customized Covenant Creation Summary
entries.summary: Overview of the covenant creation procedure: start from the baseline, choose a power level, then pick Boons and Hooks and spend Build Points on resources.
quotes: Starting from the baseline below, choose a power level

entries.title: Covenant Power Level and Build Points
entries.summary: The troupe chooses one of four power levels (low, medium, high, legendary), which sets the Build Points, the maximum level of lab texts and enchanted-device effects, and the minimum age of the covenant.

entries.title: Covenant Resource Costs in Build Points
entries.summary: Build Point costs for buying enchanted items, extra and non-standard laboratories, laboratory texts and library books (Art and Ability summae, tractatus) at covenant creation.
quotes: 2 per five levels of effects
Extra labs: 50 each
Tractatus: Quality (Quality limit: 11)

entries.title: Covenant Build Point Costs: Money, Specialists and Vis
entries.summary: Build Point costs for starting stocks of money, for specialist covenfolk (teachers and others) and for vis sources and stocks.
quotes: Sources: 5 per pawn of vis per year
Stocks: 1 per 5 pawns of vis

entries.title: Covenant Seasons
entries.summary: The Order classes covenants as Spring, Summer, Autumn or Winter according to their life stage, and many covenant features depend on that season.
quotes: The Order of Hermes traditionally classifies covenants into four seasons: Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter.

entries.title: Spring Covenants
entries.summary: Describes new, resource-poor Spring covenants, the ways a saga can start in one (from nothing, in ruins, or as a rebirth of a Winter covenant), and the style of play they give.
quotes: Spring covenants are just getting started.

entries.title: Summer Covenants
entries.summary: Describes established, still-growing Summer covenants, which suit mixed groups of experienced players and newcomers and give player characters freedom to follow their own plots.
quotes: Summer covenants are firmly established, and still growing.

entries.title: Autumn Covenants
entries.summary: Describes powerful Autumn covenants living on past glories and the two ways to play them: as junior magi under elders, or as the elder magi themselves.
quotes: An Autumn covenant is living off past glories, but has yet to go seriously into decline.

entries.title: Winter Covenants
entries.summary: Describes declining Winter covenants full of old, peculiar magi, and how a saga can pull one back to Spring or play the old magi.
quotes: Winter covenants are in decline, and on their way to oblivion.

entries.title: Base Covenant Resources
entries.summary: Three pre-built resource packages (weak, medium, powerful) that save time at covenant creation instead of using the full Customized Covenant Creation rules.
quotes: If you want to save time, just pick one for your covenant.

entries.title: Weak Covenant Resources
entries.summary: The library, Lab Texts and vis income of a weak covenant, suited to a Spring covenant or what is accessible in a Winter one.
quotes: Lab Texts: 200 levels of spells, none over level 25.
Build Points Spent: 200

entries.title: Medium Covenant Resources
entries.summary: The library, Lab Texts, vis and enchanted items of a medium covenant, suited to early Summer or young magi in an Autumn covenant.
quotes: Lab Texts: 1,000 levels of spells, none over level 40
Build Points Spent: 800

entries.title: Powerful Covenant Resources
entries.summary: The library, Lab Texts, vis and enchanted items of a powerful covenant, suited to high Summer or young magi in a very powerful Autumn covenant.
quotes: Build Points spent: 2000

entries.title: Customized Covenant Creation
entries.summary: Introduces the build-point method in which the whole troupe designs the covenant together, starting from a concept and then choosing how powerful it is.
quotes: The covenant should be created by the whole troupe, working together.

entries.title: Covenant Baseline
entries.summary: Defines the default covenant that Build Points modify: a stone building in a level 3 Magic aura with no magical resources, about one grog and two other covenfolk per magus, and Aging Modifier 0.
quotes: located in a level 3 Magic aura
The Aging Modifier for a basic covenant is 0.

versions.title: Covenant Baseline
versions.summary: Describes what a default covenant already has before any Boons, Hooks or resources are bought: its building, aura, defenses, income, labs and covenfolk.
quotes: The covenant has a Living Conditions modifier of +1 for magi and 0 for everybody else.

entries.title: Accessible Power Level
entries.summary: A table of Low, Medium, High and Legendary power levels giving the Build Points available, the maximum level of a single Lab Text or enchanted effect, and the minimum covenant age.
quotes: Maximum Level: The highest level of a single Lab Text or a single effect in an enchanted device.
Minimum Age: The minimum number of years that have passed since the foundation of the covenant.

entries.title: Library (Covenant Creation)
entries.summary: How to buy Art summae, Ability summae and tractatus with Build Points, including cost formulas and level and quality limits.
quotes: ART SUMMA COST: Level + Quality
ABILITY SUMMA COST: Quality + 3 x Level
TRACTATUS COST: Quality

entries.title: Lab Texts (Covenant Creation)
entries.summary: How covenant Lab Texts are bought with Build Points, limited by the maximum level for the power level.
quotes: LAB TEXT COST: 1 Build Point per five levels

entries.title: Casting Tablets (Covenant Creation)
entries.summary: How Casting Tablets, which let magi cast Formulaic or Ritual spells they do not know, are bought with Build Points.
quotes: Casting Tablet Cost: 2 Build Points per five levels

entries.title: Vis (Covenant Creation)
entries.summary: How vis sources and one-off vis stocks are bought with Build Points.
quotes: VIS SUPPLIES COST: 5 Build Points per pawn of vis per year
VIS STOCKS COST: 1 Build Point per 5 pawns of vis

entries.title: Enchanted Items (Covenant Creation)
entries.summary: How covenant enchanted items are bought with Build Points, with the level cap from the power level table.
quotes: Enchanted Item Cost: 2 Build Points per five levels of effect, including modifications

entries.title: Specialists (Covenant Creation)
entries.summary: How teachers and other non-magus specialists are bought for the covenant with Build Points, with costs based on their Ability scores and score limits set by age.
quotes: TEACHER COST: Communication + Teaching + Highest Ability Score
SPECIALIST COST: Highest Ability Score

related.text: ArM5 p.48 Starting Ability limits by age

entries.title: Covenant Hooks
entries.summary: Hooks are story-generating features of a covenant, Major or Minor; they give no Build Points but earn the points used to buy Boons.
quotes: A Major Hook provides three points that can be spent on Boons, while a Minor Hook provides one point.

entries.title: Minor Hooks
entries.summary: List of Minor covenant Hooks (Contested Resource, Favors, Hermetic Politics, Monster, Poverty, Protector, Regio, Rival, Road, Superiors, Urban), each worth one Boon point.
quotes: Contested Resource: Access to one of the covenant's accessible resources is contested with someone, or something, else.

entries.title: Major Hooks
entries.summary: List of Major covenant Hooks (Beholden, Castle, Monster, Mundane Politics, Poverty, Regio, Rival, Road, Superiors, Unknown, Urban), each worth three Boon points, including how an Unknown Hook is run by a player.
quotes: Unknown: An Unknown Hook is taken on by one of the players, who will act as storyguide for that aspect of the saga.

entries.title: Covenant Boons
entries.summary: Boons are covenant advantages paid for only with points from Hooks, not with Build Points.
quotes: Each Minor Boon costs one point, while a Major Boon costs three points, and they must be paid for with Hooks.

entries.title: Minor Boons
entries.summary: List of Minor Boons (Aura, Edifice, Hidden Resources, Important Building, Prestige, Regio, Seclusion, Shell Keep, Tower Keep, Wealth), each costing one Hook point.
quotes: The players may take this Boon up to seven times, for a covenant in any Magic aura up to ten.
The covenant has a Reputation score of 3 (see page 28).

entries.title: Major Boons
entries.summary: List of Major Boons (Aura, Curtain Walls and Mural Towers, Prestige, Regio, Wealth), each costing three Hook points.
quotes: The covenant has a Reputation score of 9 (see page 28).

entries.title: Resources (Vis and Books Guidelines)
entries.summary: Guidance for storyguides on how much vis and how many books to give the player characters, with Low, Moderate and High vis supply levels per magus per year and advice on handing out vis finds before vis sources.
quotes: Up to 5 pawns/magus/year.
Around 10 pawns/magus/year.
Around 20 pawns/magus/year.

entries.title: Situational Modifiers to Loyalty
entries.summary: Tables of loyalty point modifiers for living conditions, equipment quality, salary and pension, and the loyalty bonus provided by turb captain, steward and chamberlain.
quotes: Covenant grants a standard salary (standard Wages)
Covenant provides a pension upon retirement (half Wages until death)

alsoIn.title: Situational Modifiers to Loyalty (Living Conditions, Equipment, Money, Specialists)

entries.title: Familiarity
entries.summary: Covenfolk grow used to their own magi over time, gaining loyalty points each year up to a cap equal to the covenant's Gift-based base loyalty points.
quotes: For every year that a covenant exists it gains two loyalty points.

entries.title: Prevailing Loyalty
entries.summary: Introduces Prevailing Loyalty, a covenant-wide measure of how loyal and well-motivated its members are, on the same scale as Personality Traits.
quotes: It is expressed as a positive or negative number on the same general scale as Personality Traits.

entries.title: Prevailing Loyalty and Individual Loyalty
entries.summary: How an individual's Loyal to Covenant Trait relates to the covenant's Prevailing Loyalty, including how far it may deviate, and the table of Gift modifiers to Base Loyalty.
quotes: can vary by up to three points either way from the average Prevailing Loyalty of the covenant
| The Gift | –30 |
| The Blatant Gift | –105 |

entries.title: Green Covenants (Loyalty)
entries.summary: In a new covenant, or with newly recruited covenfolk, the Loyal to Covenant Trait is unlikely to exceed zero because the covenfolk distrust the Gifted until familiarity builds.

entries.title: Established Covenants (Loyalty)
entries.summary: Older covenants have usually gained enough Familiarity points for a Prevailing Loyalty of zero; large influxes of new covenfolk dilute this, and a new magus lowers Base Loyalty.
quotes: An established covenant usually has sufficient loyalty points through Familiarity (see below) to give them a Prevailing Loyalty of zero.

entries.title: Decreasing Loyalty Due to Actions and Events
entries.summary: Introduces the five categories of loyalty loss: attitude, punishments, wounds, local events and reputation.
quotes: five categories of Loyalty Point loss: attitude, punishments, wounds, local events, and reputations

entries.title: Increasing Loyalty Due to Actions and Events
entries.summary: Introduces the five ways to gain loyalty points: familiarity, altruism, rewards, local events and reputation.

entries.title: Covenant Loyalty
entries.summary: Prevailing Loyalty is the average 'Loyal to Covenant' Personality Trait of the covenant's servants, specialists and soldiers, reflecting the covenant's morale; individuals can vary a few points either way.
quotes: can vary by up to three points either way from the average Prevailing Loyalty of the covenant

entries.title: Sample Prevailing Loyalty Scores
entries.summary: Table describing the attitude of covenfolk at each Prevailing Loyalty score from -6 to +6, including productivity effects at the extremes.

entries.title: Calculating Prevailing Loyalty
entries.summary: Base Loyalty is the average of the magi's Gift modifiers; loyalty points from situation and events are added and converted to a Prevailing Loyalty score via the Ability advancement table.
quotes: BASE LOYALTY = total of Gift modifiers / number of magi

versions.title: Calculating Prevailing Loyalty (Base Loyalty)
versions.summary: Procedure for finding a covenant's Prevailing Loyalty: average the magi's Gift modifiers to get Base Loyalty, add situational loyalty points, then convert the total using the Abilities: To Buy column of the Advancement Table.
quotes: Base Loyalty: Total of Gift Modifiers / Number of Magi
converting negative loyalty points into a negative Prevailing Loyalty

entries.title: Modifying Loyalty Due to Covenant Situation
entries.summary: Wages, equipment, living conditions and competent specialists (turb captain, steward, chamberlain, or an autocrat doing two roles) all add or remove loyalty points.
quotes: The covenant can employ up to three specialists who deal with the covenfolk on their behalf

versions.title: Modifying Loyalty Due to Covenant Situation
versions.summary: Loyalty points come from equipment, wages, living conditions and from up to three specialists (turb captain, steward, chamberlain) who manage the covenfolk; modifiers that affect only part of the covenfolk are scaled down in proportion.
quotes: Magi can employ up to three specialists who deal with the covenfolk on their behalf, rather than dealing with them directly.
A single individual may perform up to two of these tasks

entries.title: Changing Loyalty Due to Actions & Events
entries.summary: Magi's actions, and local events they are blamed for, reduce loyalty more easily than they raise it; penalties apply only to events that happen in play or that the players agree happened offstage.
quotes: Unfortunately, it is easier for magi to reduce the loyalty of the covenfolk than to increase it.

entries.title: Example Loyalty Point Penalties
entries.summary: Table of loyalty point penalties (1 to 15) by severity of attitude, punishment, wound or local event.

versions.title: Example Loyalty Point Penalties
versions.summary: Table of loyalty point penalties from -1 to -15 for magi's Attitude, Punishment, Wounds dealt to covenfolk and Local Events, with notes on what each Attitude entry means.
quotes: | –1 | Rudeness | Minor Humiliation | Superficial | Minor Hardship |

entries.title: Attitude (Loyalty Penalties)
entries.summary: Extreme attitudes of the magi toward the covenfolk cost loyalty points; the penalty applies per offending magus and only the most severe penalty counts for each magus.
quotes: Only the most severe penalty applies.

entries.title: Prevailing Loyalty Example
entries.summary: Worked example calculating Base Loyalty and Prevailing Loyalty for a covenant of six magi with a turb captain and an autocrat.
quotes: Thus, the covenant has a Base Loyalty of –38 (–225 / 6).

entries.title: Punishment (Loyalty Penalties)
entries.summary: A magus ordering physical punishment of a resident causes a loyalty penalty, adjusted by the victim's Reputation and only applying to unjust punishment when Prevailing Loyalty is positive.
quotes: If dearly loved, add the Reputation to the penalty

entries.title: Wounds (Loyalty Penalties)
entries.summary: Wounds a magus deals to covenfolk cost loyalty points, one category worse if inflicted by magic, halved for accidental wounds to grogs defending the covenant, and increased by the Reputation of a dead character.
quotes: If the wound is inflicted by magic, it is treated as one category more severe.

entries.title: Local Events (Loyalty Penalties)
entries.summary: Hardships and disasters in the area lower morale even when the magi are not at fault, and the penalty persists unless the magi help resolve the event.

entries.title: Example of the Effects on Loyalty of Changing Membership
entries.summary: Worked example of how recruiting more covenfolk dilutes Familiarity points, and how adding a magus with the Blatant Gift changes Base Loyalty.
quotes: If the number of covenfolk is doubled through recruitment, the 38 loyalty points from familiarity are diluted by one-half to 19

entries.title: Reputation (Loyalty Loss)
entries.summary: A bad Reputation known to the covenfolk costs the covenant loyalty points for each point of that Reputation.
quotes: The covenant loses five Loyalty Points for every point of each such Reputation.

entries.title: Altruism (Loyalty Gain)
entries.summary: Magi who personally help covenfolk, for example by assisting in healing or taking a wound for them, earn loyalty points equal to the matching penalty, with conspicuous magic raising the gain a level.
quotes: Conspicuous use of magic in such altruistic acts increases the bonus to the next level.

entries.title: Rewards (Loyalty Gain)
entries.summary: Celebrations and a regular cycle of feast days earn the covenant loyalty points, at a cost to its wealth.
quotes: A one-off celebration after a notable event earns one Loyalty Point

entries.title: Local Events (Loyalty Gain)
entries.summary: Good fortune only raises loyalty if the magi clearly caused it; then the bonus equals the penalty that the same event would have caused.

entries.title: Reputation (Loyalty Gain)
entries.summary: A good local Reputation known to the covenfolk gives loyalty points for each point of Reputation.
quotes: then five loyalty points are gained for every point of the Reputation.

entries.title: Loyalty and Mentem Magic
entries.summary: Creo and Rego Mentem spells can create devotion, cure disloyalty or force obedience, but to change Prevailing Loyalty they must be powerful and regularly used, which causes Warping.

entries.title: Stories Caused by Prevailing Loyalty
entries.summary: A low Prevailing Loyalty produces periodic crises and acts like a Hook that is resolved by stories adding loyalty points.
quotes: A covenant with a Prevailing Loyalty score of –3 or less is prone to periodic crises of faithfulness

entries.title: Accepting Refugees: Loyalty Penalty
entries.summary: When a covenant takes in refugees from another covenant, its covenfolk suffer a loyalty penalty that is gradually reduced by stories that bring the two communities together.
quotes: the covenant suffers a Loyalty penalty of –3, as though suffering a Severe Hardship

entries.title: Vis Sources
entries.summary: Explains what a vis source is, the Art and amount of vis it normally yields, and how vis must be gathered.
quotes: Sometimes, however, it is possible to take a certain number of pawns of vis from a place every year.

entries.title: Vis Sources: Yield and Design
entries.summary: Guidance on assigning a yield to a vis source according to the saga's vis level and the importance of the story attached, and on designing sources that need a story to reach but not to harvest.
quotes: a source with a high yield should give about as much vis as an individual magus receives in a year.

entries.title: Vis Source Yields
entries.summary: Table of annual pawns of vis for low, moderate and high yield sources in low, moderate and high vis sagas.

entries.title: Vis Storage
entries.summary: Optional rule that large stockpiles of single-Art vis cause spontaneous Art-appropriate spells, with the spell magnitude growing with each multiple of the minimum stored, plus a simpler list of harmless effects per Art.
quotes: For every multiple beyond the minimum, an additional magnitude is added to the level of spells that may spontaneously occur.

entries.title: Extraordinary and Dedicated Vis Costs (Covenant Creation)
entries.summary: Build Point costs for covenant vis sources that produce extraordinary or dedicated vis, and how those costs set trade value relative to normal vis.
quotes: Dedicated Vis Source Cost: 7.5 Build Points per pawn of vis per year
divide its cost in Build Points by 5

entries.title: Style of Governance (Covenfolk)
entries.summary: A Free Choice of how the covenfolk (not the magi) are governed: autocracy, council, democracy, faux feudalism, gerontocracy, militocracy or theocracy.
quotes: Each covenant should select one of the following styles by which the residents of the covenant are governed.

entries.title: Forms of Governance
entries.summary: Describes the five basic ways a covenant can be governed (democracy, autocracy, hierarchy, bureaucracy, anarchy), who each suits, and how the styles can be combined.
quotes: There are five basic systems by which covenants may be governed

entries.title: Membership of a Covenant
entries.summary: Normally only magi are covenant members; extending membership to non-magi needs a procedure in the charter, and such members are treated as having the same rights and duties as at least some magi.

entries.title: Leadership and Offices
entries.summary: How covenant leaders are chosen or removed, why a covenant benefits from appointed officers for the library, vis, money and similar duties, and Latin titles for leaders and offices.
quotes: One very effective system is to give the casting vote (which breaks ties) to the officer under whose purview a proposal falls.

entries.title: Boons, Hooks, and Governance Styles
entries.summary: A table suggesting which Boons, Free Choices and Hooks suit each style of governance; none of the styles requires any particular Boon or Hook.
quotes: None of the styles of governance in themselves require any specific Boons or Hooks.

entries.title: The Council Meeting
entries.summary: Covers regular and extraordinary council meetings: scheduling by season or quarter day, what is decided there, and the use of a quorum so a single magus cannot decide for the whole covenant.
quotes: A quorum equal to more than half of the covenant's members is often considered reasonable.

entries.title: The Charter of Covenant
entries.summary: Explains the Oath of Covenant and the written Charter of Covenant with its bylaws, and notes that a charter notarized by a Quaesitor becomes enforceable as part of a Tribunal's Peripheral Code.
quotes: If a charter has been notarized by a Quaesitor it is legally enforceable as part of the Tribunal's Peripheral Code.

entries.title: Charter Section: Membership
entries.summary: The charter lists members and requirements for joining (usually Order membership and a council vote), and may define levels of membership or a period of servitude before full privileges.

entries.title: Charter Section: Method of Governance (Voting)
entries.summary: The charter sets out leadership, offices, how meetings and decisions work, who votes, how ties are broken (casting vote, extra vote, status quo or certamen) and how the charter may be changed.
quotes: The matter of breaking tied votes should also be addressed.

entries.title: The Charter of Arae Flaviae
entries.summary: A model democratic charter used by many young covenants; a Quaesitor's ratification is automatic if it is adopted without alteration. A blank copy is in the Appendix.
quotes: Ratification of a charter by a Quaesitor (where this is mandatory, see below) is automatic if a covenant uses the Charter of Arae Flaviae without alteration.

entries.title: Examples of Vote-Taking
entries.summary: Menu of options for running council votes: criteria for a legal meeting, methods of casting and allocating votes, ways to adjudicate a result (majority by vote, magus or member, threshold, unanimity) and types of voting.
quotes: Majority by Member: As above, but more than half of the magi who are members of the covenant must vote aye for the motion to be carried

entries.title: Charter Section: Covenant Resources
entries.summary: The charter should list what the covenant owns, to separate it from members' personal property; the text lists the kinds of resources a covenant may hold.

entries.title: Charter Section: Member Rights
entries.summary: How a charter divides covenant resources among members: basic food, shelter and laboratory, library and item access, vis sharing (and its link to the Vis Salary and Vis Grant options), money, and rewards for work done for the covenant.
quotes: Most charters allow magi to keep whatever vis they find, unless it proves to be a renewable source, in which case it belongs to the covenant.

entries.title: Charter Section: Member Obligations
entries.summary: The duties a charter places on members, such as safeguarding resources, harvesting vis and collecting income, often falling on the younger magi, plus any ad hoc obligations.

entries.title: Example of a Complex Method of Governance
entries.summary: A worked example of a council with a disceptator, quorum, categories of issue and different voting thresholds for each.
quotes: Issues of Significance require a Majority by Member to be passed

entries.title: The Carrot and the Stick (Standard Shares and Services)
entries.summary: A sample charter rule that ties each magus's annual share of covenant vis to performing Standard Services (and optional Additional Services) for the covenant.
quotes: A magus may earn up to one extra share per year by performing an Additional Service equivalent to a Standard Service.

entries.title: Obligations and the Code of Hermes
entries.summary: Explains how heavy covenant obligations interact with the Oath of Hermes ban on depriving a magus of magical power, and why a covenant may not change obligations against a magus's will.
quotes: the covenant cannot alter the obligation imposed on any magus against his will without committing a High Crime

entries.title: Censure
entries.summary: How a covenant may punish a member who breaks the charter, through expulsion or by withholding commonly held privileges, and why denying a magus his own property or laboratory breaches the Oath of Hermes.
quotes: Expulsion from the covenant is the most serious punishment a covenant can inflict.

entries.title: The Official Seal (Quaesitorial Ratification of a Charter)
entries.summary: Some Tribunals require a charter to be approved by the Quaesitores, who may add it to the Peripheral Code; a Quaesitor can only demand changes where the charter breaks the Oath of Hermes or the Peripheral Code.
quotes: No Quaesitor can dictate the contents of a charter

entries.title: Sample Covenant Charter: Oath of Covenant
entries.summary: Play aid giving the text of a fill-in-the-blanks covenant oath, taken from the charter of Arae Flaviae, which the Quaesitors will automatically ratify if adopted.
quotes: I pledge my lifelong support and loyalty to the Covenant of ...

entries.title: Charter: Membership
entries.summary: Sample charter clauses defining Protected Guests, Probationary Members and Full Members, how each is admitted, and how a member may leave.
quotes: The status of provisional member shall last a period of seven seasons, unless abridged through censure or canceled through expulsion.

entries.title: Charter: Governance
entries.summary: Sample charter clauses on the Council of Members: quorum, regular meetings, voting majorities, and the rotating office of disceptator.
quotes: The Council of Members shall convene four times each year, one day prior to each equinox and solstice
All issues shall be passed by a majority vote of the members there present
Each disceptator serves for a period of seven years, commencing one year following Tribunal.

entries.title: Charter: Resources
entries.summary: Sample charter clauses on what the covenant claims (vis, books, items, money, buildings) versus what belongs to the finder, and how surplus is determined at the Winter meeting.
quotes: This covenant lays claim to all the vis originating from undisputed and unclaimed sources discovered by members of the council; save for the first harvest of a new vis source, which belongs to the finder or finders.

entries.title: Charter: Rights of Members
entries.summary: Sample charter clauses setting out the basic rights of all members and guests, the fuller rights of Full Members, and the half-share rights and half-weight vote of Probationary Members.
quotes: a fractional share of those rights and duties offered to a full member of the covenant, such share being equal to half that offered to full members.

entries.title: Charter: Responsibilities of Members
entries.summary: Sample charter clauses on member duties: obeying the Code, minor assigned duties, paid covenant work with a minimum remuneration in vis, and the service required of probationary members.
quotes: two pawns of vis, of the flavor most prevalent in the stores at the time

entries.title: Charter: Censure and Expulsion
entries.summary: Sample charter clauses on censuring a member by vote and on expulsion, which needs a unanimous vote and is the only way to lose basic rights.
quotes: Expulsion is enacted by a unanimous vote of the remaining Council of Members.

entries.title: The Covenant Rolls
entries.summary: Records of past covenant accounts that serve as a summa for Profession: Chamberlain and a growing encyclopedia of Area Lore: Covenant, can be researched with a roll, act as an Arcane Connection to the covenant if removed, and may be incomplete or damaged.
quotes: The rolls serve as a summa for the Profession: Chamberlain Ability, typically with a Quality of 6.
make an Intelligence + Area Lore: Covenant roll with an Ease Factor related to the obscurity of the information sought

entries.title: A Noble Household
entries.summary: Lays out the household offices (steward, chamberlain, marshal and their subordinates) a large covenant can copy to organize its servants and specialists.
quotes: the three chief officials in a noble household are the steward, the chamberlain, and the marshal

entries.title: Nations (organizing covenfolk)
entries.summary: Lets a covenant divide its grogs into nations that cut across servant, specialist and soldier roles, formed by family, ethnic group or location, with members often holding a Loyalty Personality Trait specific to their nation.
quotes: The identifying feature of a nation is that it cuts across roles.

entries.title: Professional Guilds
entries.summary: Models covenant guilds on craft, service and merchant guilds, grouping those with the same or allied Craft or Profession Abilities and laying out the guild ranks from dean down to apprentices.
quotes: A guild consists of all craftsmen that use the same or a group of closely allied Craft or Profession Abilities.

entries.title: Monastery (organizing covenfolk)
entries.summary: A guild-like structure where department officials can requisition manpower and funds as needed instead of having their own permanent staff, suited to small covenants.
quotes: This is a good model for a small covenant

entries.title: The Manufacture of Books
entries.summary: Describes how a covenant produces a book, from author or notary to scribe, illuminator and binder, and the staff needed; writing speed depends on the lower of the author's and notary's totals.
quotes: The speed of this writing, as described in ArM5, page 165, is based on the Communication + Language total of either the author or notary, whichever is lower.

entries.title: Extended Quality of Books (introduction)
entries.summary: Introduces an optional, more detailed system in which a book's quality comes from author, scribe, binder and resonant materials, and can be reduced by secondary functions or damage.
quotes: This section presents a more complicated system, which allows troupes to improve covenant libraries through play and construct great tools of learning.

entries.title: Resonances and Clarification of Books
entries.summary: Resonant materials can add quality points to a book (one for purchased materials, one for materials from stories), and a third point comes from clarifying the book by enchantment and leaving it in a Magical aura; includes the sidebars on resonant components and a summary of quality rules.
quotes: A book's quality can be increased by one point if the book incorporates resonant materials that the covenant purchases.
A third point of Quality can be gained by clarifying a book.
The book must then be left in a Magical aura for (12 / aura strength) years

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material Bonus Table

entries.title: Potentially Resonant Book Components
entries.summary: List of the parts of a book (inks, pages, boards, ribbons, ornamentation, registers and so on) that can incorporate resonant materials.
quotes: The cover boards

entries.title: Summary of Quality Rules
entries.summary: Side-by-side summary of the core and extended formulas for summa and tractatus quality, including maximum quality, the effect of skilled artisans and the bonus for resonant materials.
quotes: Author's Communication + 6 + bonuses due to Virtues + bonus for writing to level less than half of Art score.
Quality may not exceed 2 x (Communication + Virtue bonuses + 6).

entries.title: Extended Quality Rules (Summa and Tractatus)
entries.summary: Extended formulas for maximum summa and tractatus quality, adding bonuses for skilled scribe, binder and illuminator and for mystical resonance, with the skill threshold for artisans and the bonus for each kind of resonant material.
quotes: A professional is considered to be skilled if she has a Profession score of 6 or more.
Resonant materials add +1 to quality if they are purchased items, +2 if they are rare items only to be gained from stories.

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material Bonus Table

entries.title: Secondary Functions of Books
entries.summary: Book variants that trade quality for another purpose (damaged, edition de luxe, epitome, ex libris, exemplar, flap-bound, holographical, huge and congregational codices, juvenilia, palimpsest, unbound), each with its own quality modifier or restriction.
quotes: An exemplar has a –3 modification to quality.
A flap book has a quality modifier of –1 and cannot have resonant materials incorporated as cover ornamentation.
For the purposes of enchantment, a book has a material level of 2 and a size multiplier of 4.
A literate person may make 15 levels of juvenile copy in a season.

entries.title: Opus Types
