entries.summary: Introduces the opus types, the styles of book that expand on the core summae and tractatus.

entries.title: Scriptoria
entries.summary: How mundane and Hermetic scriptoria work, including covenant copyists who need Magic Theory and Realm Lore to produce incorrupt copies.

entries.title: Other Opus Types
entries.summary: Rules for commentaries, correspondences, florilegia, folios, glossed books, inspeximuses, pictorial works, pamphlets and primers, including their quality bonuses, study restrictions and how they are bought at covenant creation.
quotes: A magus gains an extra experience point in each season in which he is engaged in useful correspondence.
If these minima are met, the tractatus all gain a +1 bonus to quality.
adds 1 to the quality of a book. It is performed during a season of reading.
which increases the level of his book by one-third of the difference between his current Art score and the Art score he had when he wrote the summa

entries.title: The Hermetic Book Cycle
entries.summary: Overview of the life of a book in a Hermetic library: selection, acquisition, accession, use, and deselection and disposal.
quotes: The book cycle describes the life of each book within a Hermetic library.

entries.title: Prices for Books
entries.summary: Guidance on what Hermetic and mundane books cost, mostly in pawns of vis, by quality tier (mundane, damaged, vain, sound, excellent), including the Cow and Calf Oath restricting resale or copying.
quotes: Many Hermetic books are sold under a condition called the Cow and Calf Oath.
Characters can usually purchase vain summae for half their level in pawns of vis
These charge a number of pawns of vis equal to the book's level, if the purchaser is willing to wait a season for the copy to be produced.
A surcharge of up to 20% is added if there is a spare copy available for the impatient.

entries.title: Accession
entries.summary: Accession is preparing a new book for the library through physical preparation and then classification.

entries.title: Shelf-Readying
entries.summary: The steps of preparing a book for the shelf (covering, numbering, ownership marks, vouchers, chaining); a voucher briefly acts as an arcane connection to the book it came from.
quotes: The voucher briefly acts as an arcane connection to the book, due to the law of contagion.

entries.title: Catalog as Proxy
entries.summary: A library's catalog serves as an arcane connection to the whole collection and each book in it, giving protection against botched spells; a ritual binds a library to its catalog and must be repeated if every copy is destroyed.
quotes: A magus performing it requires a season and a pawn of Vim vis.

entries.title: Study in a Library
entries.summary: Study rules assume optimal reading conditions; poor conditions can impose a quality penalty at the storyguide's discretion, and magic gives no extra mechanical advantage to a reading room.
quotes: A magus working in poor conditions suffers a quality penalty of up to –6, at the storyguide's discretion.

entries.title: Library Research
entries.summary: A magus seeking a fact in a library rolls Intelligence plus an Ability, with a bonus that depends on how strong the library's holdings on the subject are, plus any bonus from a significant magical item.
quotes: A magus seeking a fact in a library makes an Intelligence + Ability roll, with a bonus modified by the library's holdings.
+5 for a peerless collection on a subject

entries.title: Enchanted Space (Libraries)
entries.summary: Describes the functions a library enchanted as a space can provide (storage, retrieval, delivery, answers, theft prevention, structural capacity), including booby-trapped lab notes and catalogs used as proxy targets.
quotes: a magus following an uncorrected copy, who fails an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll against an Ease Factor of 12, must roll as if he had botched an experiment

entries.title: Alternatives to Books
entries.summary: Introduces the non-book study sources a covenant can collect (phenomena, information and knowledge) that magi can study from in place of books.
quotes: Students may gain an understanding of a subject from three sources.

entries.title: Significatos
entries.summary: Magically significant events or sites can give a magus study totals as if he were studying from vis, with a rule of thumb for how many pawns an event is worth and a season needed to absorb the lesson.
quotes: As a rule of thumb, an event can substitute for a number of pawns of vis equal to one-fifth (round up) of the highest Might possessed by the creatures involved.
Study takes an entire season, even if the event itself is brief

entries.title: Realia
entries.summary: Collections of mundane or magical objects are studied as a tractatus whose quality depends on the number of unique specimens, cost Build Points at covenant creation, can be divided among several students, and give a small bonus to research rolls.
quotes: A realia collection is studied as a tractatus.
Realia collections rarely rise above quality 6, which requires 32 excellent specimens.
A suitable collection of realia adds up to +1 on a research roll.
quality 1 costs one Build Point, quality 2 costs three points, three costs six points, four costs ten points, five costs 15 points, six costs 21 points.

entries.title: Alternatives to Parchment
entries.summary: Unusual media that carry text, such as a magical mirror, are treated like books for study purposes and use the same quality scale.
quotes: Alternatives to parchment are treated, for study purposes, as if they were books.

entries.title: Great Works
entries.summary: Great Works are large structures that teach like a summa or tractatus; they have a minimum cost, no scribing, binding or illumination bonuses but triple resonance and clarification bonuses, and are bought with Build Points like an equivalent book or as an Edifice Boon.
quotes: Great Works are, in game terms, created and used as summae or tractatus.
However, a Great Work costs at least 100 Mythic Pounds to build, or a similar investment of magical resources.
On the other hand, it gains triple the normal bonus from resonant materials and clarification.

entries.title: Knowledge-Based Libraries
entries.summary: Libraries made of teachers, such as ghosts or spirits, use the teaching rules rather than book study rules and are bought using the covenant creation guidelines for teachers.
quotes: Knowledge-based libraries use the teaching rules rather than the book study rules.

entries.title: Rules for a Large Library
entries.summary: A way to record a big library as a single Level and Quality per Art or Ability: the best summa gives the base score and extra summae and tractatus add experience points to Level and Quality only if they are close enough to the library's current score.
quotes: Each Art and Ability is represented as a single Level and Quality that represents the sum total of the knowledge that the library has on that subject.
A book does not contribute an experience point to Quality unless its Quality is within three points of the library Quality

entries.title: Grant of a Fair
entries.summary: Who may be granted a fair, the profit and running cost of a medium fair, and how owning a fair rates as a covenant source of income under the Minor Resources Boon.
quotes: A typical annual fair for a town counts as a Lesser Source of Income
for the Minor Resources Boon Rights

related.text: Covenants p.16 Minor Resources Boon Rights

entries.title: Prices of Goods
entries.summary: Explains the universal price table for commodities by quality, quoted in Mythic Pounds of silver per tun or ton, so players producing wealth magically can value what they create.
quotes: All prices are in Mythic Pounds of silver per tun or ton.

entries.title: Trade Weights and Measures (ton, tun, pound, yard)
entries.summary: Conversion factors between retail units for dry goods, grain, liquids and cloth and the ton or tun used for bulk prices.
quotes: 16 ounces = 1 pound = 1/2,240 ton
A tun defines the weight of a ton.

entries.title: Prices of Goods Table
entries.summary: Table of commodity prices per ton in Mythic Pounds for shoddy, standard, superior and expensive qualities, with notes on unavailable grades and goods sold by other units.

entries.title: Quality and Size Multipliers
entries.summary: Multipliers applied to price list costs for item quality and size, which stack when both apply.
quotes: | Excellent / Huge | x 5 |
something that is both Huge and of Excellent quality has a total multiplier of 25.

entries.title: Vis Notation
entries.summary: Explains the abbreviations used in vis accounting: pigni (pawns), and the occasional larger units of rooks and queens.
quotes: ten of these pawns made a "rook," and ten rooks made a "queen."

entries.title: Fortifications Free Choices (Island, Manor House, Ringwork, Small Tower)
entries.summary: Free (no-cost) fortification options: island, manor house, ringwork and small tower, noting which of them need the Castle Hook and how neighbouring nobles react to each.
quotes: Several of the Free Choices in this section require the Castle Hook.

entries.title: Castle (Major Hook)
entries.summary: Explains why a castle forces the covenant to deal with its neighbours, when the Castle Major Hook is required, and how ringworks, keeps and curtain walls relate to it.
quotes: A covenant with a castle must take the Castle Major Hook, unless the covenant has no mundane neighbors within ten miles.

entries.title: Major Fortifications Boons
entries.summary: The Major fortification Boons: curtain walls and mural towers (which include a keep, barbican and moat), a magical fortress, and superior engineering.
quotes: A curtain wall is a crenellated wall around a bailey.

entries.title: Minor Fortifications Boons
entries.summary: The Minor fortification Boons: artillery, bedrock foundations, edifices, important buildings, shell keep, tower keep, a vast and labyrinthine layout and a writ of crenellation.
quotes: Edifices do not require the Castle Hook unless several of them, grouped together, form a structure as threatening as a castle.

entries.title: Minor Fortifications Hooks
entries.summary: The Minor fortification Hooks: a crumbling castle, outbuildings clustering around it, and wooden construction.

entries.title: Tithes
entries.summary: Everyone owes the Church a tenth of income, and canon courts prosecute under-payment, a risk for Hermetic covenants that evade the tithe.
quotes: In 1220, everyone tithes a tenth of their income to the Church.

entries.title: Creating Game Statistics for a Church
entries.summary: Introduces describing a church with Build Points, Hooks and Boons in the same way a covenant is described, to show how the Church affects the saga.

entries.title: Basic Church Features
entries.summary: Explains how a church is built from Build Points, Hooks and Boons (major and minor), and gives the base Divine aura and Build Points for each kind of church from cathedral to chapel.
quotes: You may usually choose up to 10 points of Hooks for the church.
A parish church has a base Divine Aura of 4, and 250 build points.

entries.title: Resources
entries.summary: Build Point costs for a church's resources: books, enchanted items, relics priced by Faith Score and powers, specialists and vis, mostly at the same cost as for a covenant.
quotes: Enchanted Item Cost: 1 Build Point per Level of Effect
Relic Cost: Cost for Faith Score + 5 Build Points per Power

entries.title: Hooks and Boons
entries.summary: Notes that most covenant Hooks and Boons from the core rules and Covenants also suit churches, with a few new church-specific ones added.
quotes: are suitable for a church, although some may require interpretation by the troupe

entries.title: Aegis of the Hearth
entries.summary: Explains that the Aegis is the covenant-wide counterpart of Parma Magica and advises including it in a new covenant's library as a Lab Text and casting tablet.
quotes: Aegis of the Hearth (often just 'the Aegis') gives it to a whole covenant

related.text: ArM5 p.370 Aegis of the Hearth

entries.title: Aegis of the Hearth
entries.summary: The covenant's Ritual protection that works like a Parma Magica over a boundary: bars supernatural creatures with Might below its level, forces foreign effects to Penetrate it, weakens foreign castings inside, and defines natives and invitations.
quotes: No foreign supernatural creature with Might, of any type, can cross the boundary of the Aegis unless its Might exceeds the level of the Aegis.
must Penetrate a Magic Resistance equal to the level of the Aegis of the Hearth to take effect
must subtract half the level of the Aegis from any Casting Total or equivalent

entries.title: Chapter Houses
entries.summary: A chapter house lets a covenant with enough resources support additional sites. Chapters need no Tribunal approval and receive resources from the motherhouse, but are bound by the parent covenant's charter.
quotes: Chapters are not new covenants, therefore they do not require the approval of Tribunal; also, the motherhouse will provide resources for its foundation.

entries.title: Castles as Covenant Sites
entries.summary: Possessing a castle ties a covenant into feudal vassal relationships, requires a landowning knight companion, and counts as a major hook that generates stories and problems.
quotes: Castles are so obvious and party to problems that they are defined as a major hook (Covenants, page 12)

entries.title: Vassalage Between Covenants
entries.summary: Describes vassalage as the weak paying the strong for protection, and how rising mundane hostility and the spreading Dominion make good lieges more expensive and weak lieges liabilities.
quotes: Vassalage is a system in which the weak pay the strong for protection

entries.title: Covenants Held Through a Companion Knight
entries.summary: Explains how Normandy covenants cope with feudal land-holding by making a companion the nominal landholder, or by attaching to a monastery, an heiress or widow's manor, or a mercantile front, and what each choice drags into the saga.
quotes: Some have come to embrace a companion as nominal holder of their lands, thereby hoping to evade the problems of land ownership in the feudal system.

entries.title: The Receiving of Gifts
entries.summary: Each sponsor gives the new covenant a gift whose value reflects that covenant's greatness and attitude, such as books, magic items, valuables or grogs, delivered immediately or in later seasons.

entries.title: Scholae Magicae
entries.summary: Explains why schools for Gifted apprentices rarely work: Gifted children clash without a Parma Magica, Turbulences are common, mundane teachers need protection, and the Arts must be taught one-on-one.
quotes: The Hermetic Arts must be taught one-on-one, from magus to apprentice, and this limitation has yet to be overcome.

related.text: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p.33
Against the Darkness: The Transylvania Tribunal chapter 6

entries.title: Covenfolk Training Package
entries.summary: A package for people raised in a covenant; characters without exposure to Latin must move those points to other Abilities in the package.
quotes: Three Years: +5 Area Lore, +20 Area Lore: Covenant, +15 Latin, +5 Organization Lore: Order of Hermes

entries.title: Minor Covenant Boon: Chartered Town
entries.summary: A covenant boon for a covenant that is itself a chartered town, freeing it from feudal interference and taxes while burdening it with townsfolk who expect to exercise their charter rights.
quotes: This boon is incompatible with the Urban Hook (ArM5, page 74), and cannot be Unknown.

entries.title: Major Covenant Hook: Charter Lord
entries.requires: Covenant creation: Major Hook; covenant must be a large land owner
entries.summary: A covenant hook for a covenant that has granted charters to towns on its lands, drawing the attention of neighbouring lords and the Quaesitores and risking petitions or revolts from its townsfolk.
quotes: This hook may only be taken by a covenant that is a large land owner

entries.title: Major Covenant Boon: Friendly Gruagach Collective
entries.summary: A Major covenant Boon giving the covenant control over a nearby gruagach collective that supplies information, trade and aid.
quotes: This is a variant of the Hedge Tradition Covenant Boon (see Covenants page 21).

related.text: Covenants p.21 Hedge Tradition Covenant Boon

entries.title: Major Covenant Hook: Hostile Gruagach Collective
entries.summary: A Major covenant Hook where a nearby gruagach collective is hostile, spreading rumors and harvesting the covenant's vis sources.

entries.title: Minor Covenant Boon: Gruagach Ally
entries.summary: A Minor covenant Boon in which a single gruagach lives nearby and assists the magi.

entries.title: Minor Covenant Hook: Gruagach Resident
entries.summary: A Minor covenant Hook in which gruagachan live in the covenant, risking visits from a Quaesitor, curious magi and suspicious fellow gruagachan.

entries.title: Minor Covenant Boon: Mathematicus Ally
entries.summary: A Minor covenant Boon in which a university-trained mathematicus lives nearby and helps the magi.

entries.title: Minor Covenant Hook: Mathematicus Resident
entries.summary: A Minor covenant Hook in which mathematici live in the covenant, drawing Quaesitor visits if any are Gifted and visits from magi seeking Insight.

entries.title: Bear Island: Covenant Boons and Hooks for the temenos
entries.requires: Location: Bear Island temenos used as a covenant site
entries.summary: Pre-built Boons and Hooks to apply during covenant creation if the Magic temenos is the covenant site, to be adjusted as events change the island.
quotes: Boons: Major Site: Regio (Magic regio), Minor Site: Seclusion, Minor External Relations: Ungoverned, Free Fortification: Island

related.text: ArM5 Covenant creation Boons and Hooks

entries.title: Bear Island: Founding a covenant (aura choices and patron spirit)
entries.summary: Compares the three Magic aura sites on Bear Island as covenant locations and notes that covenants in the Theban Tribunal must bind a patron spirit, which could be a Daktyl or the titaness.
quotes: In the Theban Tribunal, each covenant needs to bind a patron spirit.

entries.title: Siwa Oasis Boons and Hooks
entries.summary: The Boons and Hooks that define Siwa Oasis as a covenant site, with notes on extra Hooks such as Castle, Natural Disaster and Site Hook: Regio that a troupe could add.
quotes: With seven Boons and seven Hooks, there is room for Siwa to be customized by magi living there by adding a balance of Boons and Hooks.

entries.title: New Hook: Multiple Sites
entries.requires: Covenant with important facilities at several separate sites
entries.summary: A new Resources Hook for covenants spread over several sites, covering the trade-offs of protecting each site with the Aegis of the Hearth and the threshold for the major version.
quotes: For the major form of this Hook, there are five or more sites requiring protection.

entries.title: New Hook: Fragile Vis Source
entries.requires: Covenant with a vis source of four or more pawns that can be damaged
entries.summary: A new Resources Hook describing vis sources that stop producing if a specific feature is damaged, resuming if the damage is repaired, with the threshold and counting rule for the major version.
quotes: For the major form of this Hook, there are three or more vis sites which are fragile.

entries.title: Ikhmindi Boons and Hooks
entries.summary: The Boons and Hooks that define Ikhmindi as a covenant site, including a well that benefits the Aging rolls of those who drink from it, plus suggestions for further Hooks and Boons a troupe could add.
quotes: There are six Boons and eight Hooks selected for Ikhmindi, allowing for some customization by magi establishing a covenant.

entries.title: Adulis Boons and Hooks
entries.summary: The Boons and Hooks that define the Adulis covenant site, including a Regio Hook, a healthy-feature bonus to Aging rolls, and suggestions for further Hooks such as Uncontrolled Portal and Monster.
quotes: There are four Boons and nine Hooks based on the site, allowing for some customization by magi establishing a covenant.

entries.title: New Hooks and Boons: Linked Vis Site and Unwitting Defenders
entries.requires: Covenant creation (optional new Hook and Boon)
entries.summary: Rules for two new covenant options: the Linked Vis Site Hook, where linked vis sources fail in stages if an associated condition is not met, and the Unwitting Defenders Boon, where an unaware outside force protects the covenant until the covenant reveals itself.
quotes: Their rates are halved in the first year, then quartered in the second, then stop altogether.
The vis sites thus linked must be purchased separately during covenant creation.

entries.title: Designing Tombs and Mortuaries
entries.summary: Introduces a method for designing ancient tombs with Boons, Hooks and Build Points as if they were covenants, needed only if a tomb is an ongoing part of a saga.
quotes: This section presents a method for designing ancient tombs using Boons, Hooks, and Build Points as if it were a covenant.

entries.title: Basic Tomb Features: Tether, Aura and Build Points
entries.summary: Tombs generate preternatural tethers that create Magic auras, and the tomb's rank sets its base aura and Build Points; each tomb has a cap on Hook points to spend on Boons.
quotes: For every century that a grave site (which could be a series of pyramids, or a number of individual tombs) was in use, it generates a tether score of 1, up to a maximum of 5.
Each tomb can have up to 10 points of Hooks, which can be used to purchase Boons.

entries.title: Tomb Curses as Resources
entries.summary: How to build a tomb curse as a Hermetic-style enchantment: usual Range and Target, triggers, uses per day, Greater or Lesser Malediction for effects Hermetic magic cannot copy, false curses and their Build Point cost.
quotes: Maledictions can be of any appropriate Technique or Form, and have a base level of 10 for a Lesser Malediction, and level 30 for a Greater Malediction.
A curse costs two Build Points for every five levels of effects.

entries.title: Tomb Enchanted Items: Talismans and Wards
entries.summary: Sets the Build Point cost of tomb talismans and wards and notes that they are not true Hermetic enchantments, so they can be bypassed using the trap Ease Factors, with Magic Resistance beating low Penetration automatically.
quotes: These cost two Build Points for every five levels of effects.

entries.title: Tomb Specialists
entries.summary: Tomb inhabitants such as cult priests, walking cadavers and ghostly viziers are bought as specialists, teachers or guardians for Build Points.
quotes: Tomb guardians usually cost Build Points equal to their highest Martial Ability or Brawl, as applicable.

entries.title: Tomb Traps: Build Point Costs
entries.summary: Tables giving the Build Point cost of tomb traps by severity of harm and the modifier for how hard they are to avoid.
quotes: The ease of avoiding a trap modifies the Build Point cost.

entries.title: Tomb Hooks and Boons
entries.summary: Notes how covenant Boons and Hooks apply to tombs: Wealth means intact grave goods, and Nubian tombs should take the Seclusion Boon.
quotes: In Nubia, all tombs should purchase the Seclusion Boon due to the superstitious avoidance of all things to do with the dead.

entries.title: Typical Duties of Service
entries.summary: Sample duties a vassal covenant may owe its liege: proxy sigils, directed votes, vis tithes, book copying and legacy harvesting.

entries.title: Typical Duties of Protection (and Oath Boons and Hooks)
entries.summary: Sample duties of protection a liege owes its vassals, and how oath terms translate into covenant Boons and Hooks such as Powerful Ally and Beholden.
quotes: Terms that are favorable to the vassal may give them the Powerful Ally Boon, but most oaths leave the vassal with Hooks such as Beholden.

entries.title: Breaking Free (Escaping an Oath of Fealty)
entries.summary: How a vassal covenant can end its oath, by defaulting on duties and being convicted or by prosecuting its liege, with a table of suitable Boons and Hooks for liege and vassal.
quotes: To gain independence from a liege, a vassal covenant must either wait for its liege to default on the oath of fealty, or deliberately break it themselves, since either party can cancel the oath following a successful prosecution.

entries.title: Liege & Vassal Covenants
entries.summary: Describes the usual way new Normandy covenants form, as vassals of a covenant holding a legacy, and the five great lines of liege covenants.
quotes: The vassal covenant is established within a day's march of the legacy, and ownership of the vis source passes from the liege covenant to the vassal, which may then register it as a seisin at the next Tribunal meeting.

entries.title: Oaths of Fealty
entries.summary: How covenant-to-covenant oaths of fealty work: duty of support from the vassal, duty of protection from the liege, legal enforceability, and how an oath can be dissolved.
quotes: Oaths of fealty between vassal and liege covenants are part of Normandy's Peripheral Code and legally enforceable, although covenants are still forbidden to take oaths of fealty to a mundane lord.

entries.title: The Perthean Compact and New Covenants
entries.summary: Optional guidance for limiting Build Points spent on vis when creating a Normandy covenant, and for founding a covenant with legacies or tropaea instead of seisins.
quotes: but 3 to 5 Build Points per magus to be spent on vis is reasonable.

entries.title: Minor Resources Hook: Vis Lease
entries.summary: A covenant Hook for a vis source that is only leased (legacy or tropaeum), forcing the covenant to campaign or compete at Tribunal to keep it; may be taken multiple times.
quotes: One of the covenant's vis sources is a legacy or a tropaeum rather than a seisin.

entries.title: Founding a New Covenant (Normandy Requirements)
entries.summary: The legal requirements for a new Normandy covenant: exclusive vis supply of a set minimum, a recognized council chamber at a safe distance from other covenants, and no use of chapter houses to dodge the Compact; vis from the local aura counts only as stock.
quotes: The only legal requirement is that the nascent covenant has exclusive access to one or more sources of vis that collectively supply a minimum of one pawn of vis per year for every magus in the new covenant (or at least four pawns per year, if there are fewer than four magi).
Vis extracted from the local aura does not count as a vis supply but as vis stocks

entries.title: Siting a Covenant in Brittany
entries.summary: Guidance on placing a player covenant in sparsely populated Brittany: many unclaimed vis sources and sites, but the covenant must still fit into or evade the feudal and Church structure.
quotes: Brittany is the least-civilized, most sparsely populated part of the Tribunal, with many unclaimed vis resources.

entries.title: The Covenant Patrons
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Every Theban covenant has a supernatural patron in a pact of mutual protection, represented by a Powerful Ally or Local Ally Boon, and the covenant expires if it lacks a patron.
quotes: expressed as either the Powerful Ally Boon or the Local Ally Boon
a covenant without a patron is deemed to have itself expired

entries.title: The Ceremony of Propitiation
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Procedure at Delos by which covenants offer vis or treasure to their patrons, which grants the patron experience offset by its Might, with vis offered counting like eaten vis.
quotes: Any patron who is propitiated in the rite gains 25 experience points
reducing the penalty due to the patron's Might by two points per pawn

entries.title: Dryops: a patron that pays Might for regiones
entries.summary: Explains how the covenant's spirit patron created the ships' regiones at a permanent cost to its own Might, and the debt this creates for the covenant.
quotes: Every time the spirit uses its Regio power, it permanently loses 15 points from its Might.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, pages 52 and 103

entries.title: Beasts as Characters
entries.requires: Playing a beast or enchanted animal as a character
entries.summary: Explains how beast characters are built: each species has unbalanced species Virtues and Flaws, exceptional beasts may add balanced individual ones, and normal beasts can improve existing Abilities but only learn new ones if trained, while intelligent beasts advance normally.
quotes: Normal Beasts cannot learn new Abilities unless Trained, but can improve existing Abilities; intelligent beasts can improve as normal.

entries.title: Durenmar covenfolk: Warping from the strong Magic aura
entries.requires: Covenfolk of Durenmar (covenant in a strong Magic aura)
entries.summary: Durenmar's servants and grogs are shaped by life in a strong Magic aura: each has Warping-derived Minor Flaws, and the very old gain a Supernatural Ability Virtue. A model for generating covenfolk of any covenant that lives in a strong aura.
quotes: All covenfolk have at least one Minor Flaw due to Warping, and those over 30 years old have two.

entries.title: Crintera covenfolk: the six animal clans
entries.requires: Covenant of House Bjornaer (Crintera) or a similar heartbeast-themed turb
entries.summary: Organizes the grogs and covenfolk of Crintera into six animal clans mirroring the Elders' seats, each with a role, preferred weapons and a clan leader; shows how to build a themed turb whose warriors share a heartbeast style.
quotes: The grogs and covenfolk are divided into six clans, named just as the six seats of the Elders.

entries.title: Creating a Coven
entries.requires: Saga set in a folk witch coven
entries.summary: A coven can be built with the Customized Covenant Creation rules, either as the saga's focus or as an antagonist, following a few adjustments.

entries.title: Guidelines for a Coven
entries.requires: Saga set in a folk witch coven
entries.summary: Covenant creation adjustments for dispersed covens: separate auras per site, Hooks and Boons balanced over the whole coven, vis sources assigned to individuals, initiation scripts bought with Build Points equal to their bonus, and Build Point ranges by power level.
quotes: By default, the coven has a single site with a level-3 aura
Each initiation script costs a number of Build Points equal to the script bonus.

entries.title: Option: Extremely Complex Wealth Management
entries.summary: Optional rule to track covenant finances down to shillings and pence, suited to very poor covenants or mundane/trade-focused sagas.
quotes: you may keep track of the covenant's finances exactly, recording income and expenditure down to the level of shillings and pence.

entries.title: Option: No Wealth Management
entries.summary: Optional rule to skip bookkeeping entirely and let the storyguide introduce surpluses and shortfalls by judgment, suited to very rich covenants or high fantasy sagas.

entries.title: Keep Alternatives for Castles with Curtain Walls
entries.requires: Boon: Curtain Walls and Mural Towers
entries.summary: Four alternatives to a tower or shell keep that a castle with curtain walls may choose at no extra cost: hall keep, courtyard castle, gatehouse keep and chemise.

entries.title: Barbicans and Moats
entries.requires: Boon: Curtain Walls and Mural Towers
entries.summary: Defines what a barbican and a moat are for game purposes and how a covenant obtains them, free with Curtain Walls and Mural Towers or otherwise as Edifices or Important Buildings.
quotes: A moat is a body of water at least twenty feet wide and six feet deep that surrounds the covenant.

entries.title: Prevailing Loyalty with Non-magus Members
entries.requires: Non-magus members with real votes on the ruling council
entries.summary: Unmagical council members count as zero points in the Base Loyalty average, raising it, but only if their votes are equal to those of Gifted members.
quotes: Each unGifted member of the Council contributes zero points to the calculation of Base Loyalty

entries.title: Loyalty Versus Discipline (Prevailing Discipline)
entries.summary: Optional rule that tracks Prevailing Discipline like Prevailing Loyalty, so that harsh punishment can raise discipline while lowering loyalty and indulgence does the reverse.
quotes: Maintaining Prevailing Discipline requires all specialists managing the covenfolk to use Leadership rather than their Profession Ability to maintain order.

entries.title: Fengheld's Chapter Houses (covenant chapter rules)
entries.requires: A covenant that has founded chapter houses
entries.summary: Explains how a covenant can be spread over several sites as chapter houses: all chapters remain part of the main covenant, share its charter and Tribunal rulings, and may add a local charter for their own residents. The sidebar also suggests how a player covenant can become one of the chapters.
quotes: All magi must accept the charter of Fengheld, and any strictures or rulings from the Tribunal that apply to Fengheld also apply to the chapter houses (and vice versa).
a chapter usually has a local charter that applies only to those magi who live in the chapter house

entries.title: Sample Oath of Fealty Between Covenants
entries.summary: Presents a worked example of the terms of an oath of fealty between a liege covenant and its Mercere House vassal, covering mutual aid, voting, tithes, hospitality and non-competition, along with the Tribunal's Evangelium who reports Tourney results.
quotes: Dragon's Rest will pay a tithe of one pawn of vis per year per member to Confluensis.

entries.title: The Founding of Covenants
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Requirements for founding a Theban covenant: a declared purpose, a willing patron at the site and a charter reviewed by the Conciliatory Board, then a decree of founding at Tribunal.
quotes: a prospective covenant needs a patron at the proposed site of the new covenant

entries.title: Durenmar guest laboratories and vis fees
entries.summary: Describes the fee in vis a covenant may charge a visiting magus of suitable rank for a season in its guest laboratories, with a cheaper rate for the small standard labs; a model for pricing guest lab use.
quotes: albeit with a charge of at least five pawns of vis
for the lesser fee of two pawns of vis per season each

entries.title: Allies to the Order (hedge allies of covenants)
entries.requires: Covenant or magus allied with a hedge tradition
entries.summary: How to represent hedge-tradition allies of a covenant or a single magus with Covenant Boons and Virtues such as Social Contacts and Personal Vis Source.
quotes: Minor Virtue Social Contacts (ArM5, page 49)

entries.title: Hiring Scribes at the Scriptorium
entries.summary: Visiting magi can hire some of the permanent scribes to copy books, paying vis and materials; Tremere may requisition scribes free. Gives the scribes' Ability scores.
quotes: It costs 2 pawns of vis to hire a scribe for a season
up to two scribes can be hired by visiting magi to copy books

entries.title: Kezdö Válasz Forts (relocation)
entries.summary: Describes the oppidum's forts, their staffing, the periodic relocation cycle, and the time and casting tablets used to establish or destroy a fort and move laboratories.
quotes: establishing the fort can take one to two seasons
Currently there are four active forts in the Tribunal, each home to two magi.

entries.title: Atsingani: Limits of a Mobile Covenant
entries.summary: Lists the drawbacks of a covenant without a permanent base: no stable income, no fortifications, only poor shared tent laboratories, and a single fixed vis source.
quotes: can only establish rather poor temporary laboratories (apart from the one belonging to Viviana) in tents, which they share

entries.title: The Enchanted Ships of Favonius (ship statistics and bonuses)
entries.summary: Gives the Quality, Size, damage levels and navigation and ship-handling bonuses of the covenant's four enchanted ships, and notes they are bought with the Magical Fortress Boon without spending Build Points on enchantments.
quotes: Because of the quality of workmanship, pilots receive a +2 to any navigation rolls, and captains receive a +2 bonus to any ship-handling rolls.
These ships are bought with the Magical Fortress Boon, and their enchantments do not cost covenant Build Points.

entries.title: Teaching Duties at the Scholomance
entries.summary: Sets the teaching obligations of the oppidum's magi, including the requirement that they extend their Parma Magica around pupils so The Gift does not affect them.
quotes: Magi are expected to spend one season a year teaching
Magi are required to extend their Parma around those they teach to negate the social effects of The Gift.

entries.title: Company Neighborhood (warehouses and guards)
entries.summary: Costs and staffing for a trading house's warehouse and the neighborhood built around it, including guards per ton of cargo and the season a factor spends supervising construction.
quotes: Replacing a warehouse costs 10 pounds per hundred tons of cargo storage space.
most warehouses hire one guard for every ten tons of cargo

entries.title: Minor Covenant Hook: Zenodochium
entries.summary: A covenant creation hook placing a zenodochium within a day's travel, with the covenant's duty to replace what it uses and the consequences of damage or visiting injured magi.
quotes: The covenant may freely make use of the zenodochium, but must replace any vis or other items that are used or removed.
